description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Delaware Senator Chris Coons (D) criticizes President Trump's handling of the Iran conflict as "chaotic" and costly. Mick Mulvaney, former Acting White House Chief of Staff, says only President Trump can resolve the DHS funding impasse by making clear to Republicans what he’ll accept, while warning executive actions can’t fund TSA “forever.” Heather Conley, Nonresident Senior Fellow at the American Enterprise Institute, says there is no clear negotiating track with Iran.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: White House Urges Congress to Cancel Recess | Balance of Power: Late Edition 03/30/2026

author: Fiona MacDonald, Sherif Tarek
description: Iran hit a fully laden Kuwaiti oil tanker in the anchorage area of Dubai’s port, damaging the hull and starting a fire on board, state-run Kuwait Petroleum Corp. said in a statement.
title: Iran Strikes Fully Laden Kuwait Oil Tanker in Dubai Port

author: Emily Birnbaum
description: A former top aide to President Donald Trump is initiating a $100 million campaign to promote the administration’s pro-artificial intelligence agenda during this year’s midterm elections.
title: Group Plans $100 Million Midterm Effort to Back Trump AI Agenda

description: Heather Conley, Nonresident Senior Fellow at the American Enterprise Institute and former Deputy Assistant Secretary of State for European and Eurasian Affairs under President George W. Bush, says there is no clear negotiating track with Iran. She stresses the US must clearly define its objectives to shape any path to negotiations and determine the scope of allied involvement, noting NATO support depends on mission clarity. She speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Conley Urges US to Clarify Objectives on Iran

author: Melos Ambaye
description: Republican senators on Monday unveiled a bill to stop US crypto mining companies from using equipment tied to China and other foreign adversaries.
title: Proposed GOP Bill Targets Foreign Crypto Mining Hardware

description: Senator Chris Coons, a Democrat from Delaware, says the IRGC has a firm grip on Iran still. He also says trying to take Kharg Island would be difficult and dangerous. He speaks on Balance of Power. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Taking Kharg Island Would Be Difficult, Dangerous, Says Sen. Coons

author: Anthony Capaccio
description: Key details about US military spending for the 2027 fiscal year — including the planned budgets for each of the military services — will be released on April 21, according to a US defense official, who requested anonymity to disclose the information.
title: US to Release Defense Budget Details for Fiscal 2027 on April 21

author: James Mayger
description: Australia’s parliament agreed to establish an inquiry into taxes paid by gas companies, to be led by a senator from the Greens party, a minor political group that has advocated higher levies on liquefied natural gas exports.
title: Australia Launches Gas Tax Review as War Fuels LNG Windfall

description: Mick Mulvaney, former Acting White House Chief of Staff, says only President Trump can resolve the DHS funding impasse by making clear to Republicans what he’ll accept, while warning executive actions can’t fund TSA “forever.” On Iran, he calls Trump’s mixed messaging “strategic ambiguity,” saying it’s intentional to keep adversaries guessing. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Mulvaney Says Trump Must Step In to End DHS Standoff

description: Delaware Senator Chris Coons, who serves on the Senate Foreign Relations and Appropriations Committees, criticizes President Trump's handling of the Iran conflict as "chaotic" and costly. He also addresses the DHS funding standoff, calling it a "pickle" for Senate and House Republicans navigating competing approaches. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Sen. Coons Calls Trump Iran Approach 'Chaotic'

author: Myles Miller
description: A Federal Emergency Management Agency contractor installed with backing from a key Trump ally is under investigation by the Department of Homeland Security’s inspector general over her role in approving contracts and influencing disaster funding decisions typically reserved for government officials, according to people familiar with the matter.
title: DHS Inspector General Probes FEMA Contractor’s Role in Contracts

author: Thomas Seal
description: The US won’t allow Chinese electric cars from Canada to enter its market, President Donald Trump’s ambassador in Ottawa said, after a January deal in which Prime Minister Mark Carney lowered tariffs on those vehicles.
title: Chinese Cars Can’t Cross From Canada to US, Trump’s Envoy Says

description: On today's episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec speak with Bloomberg Middle East reporter Dan Williams about President Trump's threat to bomb Kharg Island if Iran doesn't open the Strait of Hormuz and fighting in Lebanon as the war widens. Then, Florian Ielpo, head of macro at Lombard Odier Investment, breaks down the macro environment as war sends shockwaves through the global economy. Plus, Retired Marine Corps Major General Mastin Robeson discusses why securing the Strait of Hormuz not be possible even with American boots on the ground and the war's impact on the US relationship with China. Finally, Tim Baker, head of FX Research for Americas at Deutsche Bank, talks the war's impact on the strength currencies, including the US dollar and the euro. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Oil Supply Shock Roils Global Economy as US Expands Threat | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 3/30/2026

author: Ted Mann, John Harney
description: The president’s mixed messages have financial markets gyrating.
title: Trump Touts Both Talks and Threats in War With Iran

author: Alex Wickham, Ben Bartenstein
description: Iran is pushing the Houthis to prepare for a renewed campaign against Red Sea shipping, contingent upon any further escalation by the US in its war on the Islamic Republic, according to European officials familiar with the matter.
title: Iran Presses Houthis on Red Sea Shipping, European Officials Say

author: Eric Martin
description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the US may need to reassess its relationship with NATO after the Iran war is finished, calling the military alliance’s alleged lack of support during the Middle East conflict “very disappointing.”
title: US May ‘Reexamine’ NATO’s Merit After Iran War Snub, Rubio Says

author: Martha Viotti Beck, Rachel Gamarski, Matheus Piovesana
description: Banco do Brasil SA is weighing fresh financial relief for farmers hit by the war in Iran, a move that risks straining its balance sheet and reviving the need for asset sales or a capital increase.
title: Banco do Brasil Weighs Farmer Relief Amid War, Capital Risk

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondent Joe Mathieu discusses the latest from the Middle East and the White House. On today's show, Michael Allen, Managing Director of Beacon Global Strategies and Former-Special Assistant to President George W. Bush; Bloomberg Politics contributors Rick Davis, Partner at Stonecourt Capital, and Jeanne Sheehan Zaino, Democracy Visiting Fellow at Harvard Kennedy School's Ash Center; and Cliff Young, Ipsos US Public Affairs Chair and Professor at Texas A&M University’s Bush School of Government and Public Service. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Warns Iran of Escalation | Balance of Power: Early Edition 3/30/2026

author: Jim Wyss
description: Russia’s delivery of crude to fuel-starved Cuba temporarily staves off a full-blown humanitarian crisis, with other countries trying to parse Donald Trump’s decision to allow the shipment to reach the island.
title: Russian Oil Shipment Buys US and Cuba Time as Crisis Festers

description:
Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz speak with Cliff Young, Ipsos US Public Affairs Chair and Professor at Texas A&M University’s Bush School of Government and Public Service. 

Oil prices rose after President Donald Trump threatened attacks on Iran’s energy infrastructure, overshadowing his comments that a deal to end hostilities in the Middle East could be close. 
West Texas Intermediate futures rose more than 3% to trade near $103 a barrel, while the most active June Brent futures climbed to trade above $107 a barrel. 
Brent futures were volatile amid thin liquidity, with traders increasingly staying on the sidelines to avoid extreme headline-driven price swings. Front-month May futures fluctuated as investors closed out those positions ahead of the contract’s expiration on Tuesday — the price was near $112 a barrel.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Price of Gas Central to Midterm Elections, Ipsos's Cliff Young

author: Nicola M White
description: US Senator Richard Blumenthal wants Securities and Exchange Commission Chairman Paul Atkins to explain the sudden resignation of its enforcement director and whether her departure was related to cryptocurrency cases, including one touching on the Trump family’s ventures.
title: Senator Queries SEC on Crypto After Enforcement Head Quits

author: Jennifer A Dlouhy
description: The White House threatened further escalation of attacks on Iran, including critical civilian energy infrastructure, as the fifth week of war jolts global markets with little sign of relief.
title: US Expands Threats to Iran Energy, Water Even as It Hails Talks

author: Lucy White
description: The Greens have already lured away much of Labour’s support in public opinion polls. Now, they’re looking to court a sector that has long been the key source of money and manpower for the British governing party: trade unions.
title: Greens Seek to Woo UK Trade Unions in Threat to Labour Base

description: Iran sees Trump’s talk of a deal as a ruse to prepare for a decisive assault, explains Bloomberg Opinion columnist Marc Champion. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: What the Iran War Is Really About

description: The European Union's antitrust chief, Teresa Ribera, talks about how the continent is looking at the future of artificial intelligence and the importance of keeping an open, competitive market in the digital sector. She speaks to Bloomberg's Dani Burger. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Europeans Share Concerns About AI, Says Top Regulator

author: Emily Birnbaum
description: Americans are increasingly turning against artificial intelligence, with growing majorities saying they fear the fast-moving technology will take away their jobs and hurt education, according to a new Quinnipiac poll.
title: More Than Half of US Says AI Likely to Harm Them, Poll Finds

author: Jenni Thier
description: Germany can impose more than €60 billion ($68.8 billion) in cost cuts in its healthcare system by 2030 with measures such as restricting doctors’ pay, reining in drug costs and shifting the financing for welfare recipients.
title: Germany Eyes €60 Billion in Potential Healthcare Cost Cuts

author: Ellen Milligan
description: Reopening the Strait of Hormuz to commercial shipping is “easier said than done,” UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer warned ahead of a meeting designed to secure that aim once the conflict in Iran has ended.
title: Reopening Hormuz Is ‘Easier Said Than Done,’ Starmer Says

description: NASA plans on launching the Artemis II mission from Cape Canaveral in Florida on Wednesday. Four astronauts will travel in an Orion capsule into orbit and then slingshot past the moon. Bloomberg's Loren Grush is at Kennedy Space Center with more.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Why NASA Is Spending Billions to Get Back to the Moon

author: Sam Dagher
description: For Saudi Arabia, being caught in the middle of the war between Iran and its archfoes Israel and the US is the realization of a nightmare scenario the kingdom has long dreaded. The country, which sees itself as the economic and political leader of the Arab world and a beacon for Muslims everywhere, has long regarded Iran as a rival — and as a threat, one the previous Saudi king repeatedly asked the US to take on. But after the US did just that, Saudi Arabia has been alarmed to find itself dragge
title: What Does Saudi Arabia Want from the Iran War? Will It Join?

author: Lillianna Byington
description: Senate Republicans plan to fund the Department of Homeland Security for three years using a party-line budget process in an effort to sidestep Democratic opposition as the shutdown drags on, a key GOP senator said Monday.
title: GOP Plans Three-Year DHS Funding Without Democrats, Senator Says

description:
Bloomberg Canada Reporter Derek Decloet discusses the decision of Air Canada's CEO to step down after a controversial English-only video statement about the deadly runway collision at LaGuardia. 

Air Canada Chief Executive Officer Michael Rousseau announced he’s leaving after creating a public relations fiasco with an English-language video about the deadly runway collision at LaGuardia Airport in New York.
Rousseau, 68, will retire by the end of the third quarter, Air Canada said in a statement Monday morning.
An Air Canada Express jet flew from Montreal to New York on March 22 and, after landing, collided with an airport fire truck, killing both pilots. Rousseau made a video statement in which he expressed his “deepest sorrow for everyone affected.” But the only words he spoke in French were “bonjour” at the beginning and “merci” at the end. French subtitles were provided.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Air Canada CEO to Quit After Furor About Crash Condolence Video

author: Jenny Che, Nayla Razzouk
description: France detained two more people on Monday in connection with the foiled bombing attack near the Bank of America Corp. office in Paris that authorities say was likely linked to the conflict in the Middle East.
title: France Holding Five in Custody After Foiled BofA Bombing

author: Lydia Beyoud, Loukia Gyftopoulou
description: Companies offering alternative assets in retirement savings plans would get more legal protection under a new Trump administration proposal, potentially opening up opportunities for firms like Blackstone Inc. and Apollo Global Management Inc. in the $14 trillion market.
title: Private Equity Would Get Easier Path to 401(k)s In US Proposal

author: Eric Martin
description: The US Embassy in Venezuela is formally resuming operations Monday, the latest step in the Trump administration’s plan to spur the nation’s economic recovery and eventual democratic transition.
title: US Embassy in Venezuela Formally Reopens as Trump Plan Advances

description: President Donald Trump spoke to Bloomberg's Annmarie Hordern on the phone Monday morning, telling her that Iran wants to settle and that the war is going "unbelievably well." Earlier in a Truth Social post, Trump repeated threats to destroy Iran's energy assets if the Strait of Hormuz isn't reopened soon. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says Iran Really Wants to Settle the War

author: Daniel Flatley
description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent indicated optimism about a reopening of the Strait of Hormuz for passage of cargo ships and said the administration is steadily moving to address the shortage of global oil supplies.
title: Bessent Says US to ‘Retake’ Hormuz Strait Control, Eyes Escorts

author: Aliaksandr Kudrytski
description: Volodymyr Zelenskiy said Kyiv has been urged by some of its global partners to scale back attacks on Russian oil infrastructure following turmoil on global energy markets.
title: Zelenskiy Urged to Curtail Russia Energy Strikes, Proposes Truce

author: Matthew Malinowski
description: Less than three weeks into his term, polls show Chilean President José Antonio Kast’s support is tumbling amid a backlash to the biggest fuel-price increases since at least 1980 and mounting street protests.
title: Chile President Kast Sees Support Tumble in New Polls as Protests Grow

description: US President Trump renewed his threat to destroy Iran's energy sites if the Strait of Hormuz stays effectively closed. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Renews Threat on Iran Energy Sites If Hormuz Stays Closed

author: Gerry Doyle
description: After a weekend with some of the heaviest Iranian ballistic missile attacks on Gulf targets since the war began, increasingly effective strikes have consumed at least 2,400 interceptors — a number approaching those countries’ known prewar stockpiles.
title: Sustained Iran Missile Attacks Add Pressure on US to Defend Gulf

description: President Donald Trump threatened to target energy sites in Iran if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed in a post Monday on Truth Social. Trump said, “we will conclude our lovely ‘stay’ in Iran by blowing up and completely obliterating all of their Electric Generating Plants, Oil Wells and Kharg Island.” Joumanna Bercetche reports on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Renews Iran Energy Threat If Hormuz Doesn’t Reopen Soon

author: Hadriana Lowenkron
description: The Trump administration will resume processing some asylum claims after a near-blanket halt of immigration paperwork for hundreds of thousands of people seeking refuge in the US, according to a person familiar with the plans.
title: US Resumes Asylum Claims Paused After National Guard Shooting

author: Jack Wittels
description: Tankers that were carrying diesel toward Europe have switched course in the Atlantic, another sign of the global tug-of-war for increasingly tight fuels as the Iran war disrupts supply chains.
title: Tankers Carrying Diesel Toward Europe Change Course in Atlantic

author: Daniel Basteiro
description: Spain closed its airspace to American flights involved in its military operation in Iran, expanding an effort to distance itself from the conflict.
title: Spain Shuts Airspace to US Flights Involved in Iran Offensive

author: Courtney Subramanian, Magan Crane
description: President Donald Trump threatened to destroy Iran’s energy infrastructure if no deal is reached to end the war there, while also hailing talks as productive.
title: Trump Threatens Iran Energy Sites If No Deal Reached on War

author: William Horobin
description: French Finance Minister Roland Lescure said a meeting of Group of Seven finance and energy officials on Monday will take stock of the economic and financial shock from the Iran war.
title: G-7 Finance and Energy Officials Meet on Impact of Iran War

author: Tarek El-Tablawy, Salma El Wardany
description: Egyptian President Abdel-Fattah El-Sisi appealed to his US counterpart Donald Trump to find a way to end to an Iran war that’s sent global energy prices soaring and threatens developing nations’ economies.
title: Egypt’s President Appeals to Trump to Bring Iran War to an End

author: Jonathan Tamari
description: The biggest question hanging over the president this week is whether he sends in ground troops
title: Trump’s Next Big Decision in Iran Poses Huge Risks

author: Alicia A. Caldwell
description: Democratic lawmakers are starting an investigation into the Trump administration’s plan to spend billions of dollars buying and retrofitting warehouses as immigrant detention centers, ramping up scrutiny of a key piece of the White House’s push for mass deportations.
title: Democrats Probe Trump’s $38 Billion Plan for Immigrant Jails

description: President Trump says Iran has given the US most of the 15 demands to end the war even as it remains unclear whether either side is negotiating. William Roebuck, Executive Vice President at the Arab Gulf States Institute and a former US Ambassador to Bahrain spoke to Bloomberg’s Horizons Middle East and Africa anchor Joumanna Bercetche about the US ground troops in the Mideast. (Source: Bloomberg)

author: Milda Seputyte
description: Exiled Belarusian opposition leader Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya called on the European Union to maintain sanctions against her country’s authoritarian regime as she warned against following an easing of US policy toward Minsk.
title: Belarus Opposition Urges EU to Keep Sanctions Despite US Shift

author: Carla Samon Ros
description: A conservative tycoon and devout Catholic who made his fortune running luxury hotels and trains is among the frontrunners to be Peru’s next president, pledging to crack down on abortion, crime and migration.
title: Conservative Tycoon ‘Porky’ Leads Peru’s Presidential Race

author: Peter Martin
description: The conflict with Iran is reinforcing the appeal of nuclear weapons.
title: States Weigh Whether Nukes Can Bring Safety

author: Weilun Soon, Prejula Prem
description: Israel and US strikes have wiped out senior Iranian leaders and hit key targets across the country. But after a month of fighting, it is arguably Iran that has secured the most significant strategic victory — a tightening grip over traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.
title: Iran’s Grip on Hormuz Is Tighter Than Ever After a Month of War

description: Portuguese Finance Minister Joaquim Miranda Sarmento discusses the economy, its ability to withstand the impact of the war in the Middle East, and interest from airlines for a stake in TAP SA. He speaks on Bloomberg Television.
title: Portugal Well-Positioned to Bear Impact of War: Minister

author: Veena Ali-Khan, Alex Longley, Rakteem Katakey
description: One thing that’s helped to limit the damage in oil markets since the Iran war largely shuttered the Strait of Hormuz is the availability of an alternative route for getting crude from Saudi Arabia to Asia: the Red Sea.
title: How Yemen’s Houthis Could Worsen the Oil Crisis

author: Patrick Sykes, Dana Khraiche
description: US and Israeli forces pressed ahead with attacks on Iran while the Islamic Republic launched missiles across the Persian Gulf, sending oil prices higher once again amid no sign of an imminent peace deal.
title: US, Israel Keep Up Strikes on Iran With No End of War in Sight

author: Bastian Benrath-Wright, Isabel Demetz
description: People in Switzerland are encountering increasing frustration that they can’t withdraw and use cash as much as they used to.
title: Swiss Find They Can’t Pay With Cash as Much as They Used to

description: Missile strikes ripped across the Middle East over the weekend as the arrival of a US amphibious assault group and the entry of Iran-backed Houthi forces heightened fears of an escalating war. Bloomberg's Joumanna Bercetche reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Troop Buildup in Middle East Spurs Escalation Concern

author: Ana Monteiro
description: South Africa appointed career diplomat Thabo Thage as its so-called minister plenipotentiary to Washington as it finalizes the selection of a permanent ambassador, Business Day reported.
title: South Africa Appoints Thage to Embassy in Washington, BD Says

description: HSBC CEO Georges Elhedery joins Francine Lacqua to explain why he is “ruthless about killing complexity” as he pushes through an AI-fueled overhaul of one of the world’s biggest banks. He reflects on leadership, integrity and cultural fluency, and shares how HSBC is adapting to geopolitical tensions, shifting trade routes and the rapid rise of generative AI. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: HSBC CEO Interview: Georges Elhedery on AI and 'Killing Complexity' at the Bank

author: Galit Altstein
description: Israel’s central bank is set to hold interest rates steady for a second consecutive time as the US-Israeli attacks on Iran keep fueling global and domestic inflation concerns.
title: Israel to Hold Rates, Lower Growth Forecast as Iran War Persists

author: Patpicha Tanakasempipat
description: Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul is close to unveiling a new cabinet lineup, handing him more power to deal with the challenges posed by the Middle East crisis, which is threatening the Southeast Asian nation’s growth outlook.
title: Thai PM Readies New Cabinet as Energy Crisis Threatens Growth

author: Shoko Oda
description: Japan’s prime minister sought to address public concerns about a shortage of medical devices caused by the war in the Middle East, saying her government was working to ensure stable supply.
title: Japan PM Seeks to Ease Concerns Over Medical-Product Supplies

author: Galit Altstein
description: Israel’s parliament approved a 2026 state budget with a large defense supplement to cover the war with Iran, to be funded by additional borrowing and cuts in civilian spending.
title: Israel Approves Revised War Budget Extending Reliance on Debt

author: Weilun Soon
description: The true location of ships trapped in the Persian Gulf is becoming clearer after electronic interference of signals eased over the weekend, helping to reduce concerns about navigating vessels in the war-affected region.
title: Persian Gulf Ships Show True Locations as Signal Jamming Eases

author: Irina Anghel
description: Thanim Rahman had every reason to smile when his LinkedIn profile picture was taken in September 2025.
title: Why Young People Can’t Find a Job in London Anymore

author: Colum Murphy, Alastair Gale
description: China has imposed sanctions on Japanese politician Keiji Furuya, ratcheting up tension with its neighbor by accusing the lawmaker of cultivating ties with people it considers separatists in Taiwan — the island Beijing claims as its territory.
title: China Sanctions Japanese Lawmaker in Protest of His Taiwan Links

author: Soo-Hyang Choi
description: South Korea may widen restrictions on driving to include the general public if oil prices breach $120 a barrel as it seeks to cushion the impact of the Iran war on its energy supplies, the country’s finance minister said.
title: South Korea Weighs First Driving Curbs in 35 Years on Oil Crunch

author: Yian Lee
description: China has invited the leader of Taiwan’s opposition party to visit the mainland next month, the first such trip by a sitting leader of the Kuomintang since 2016.
title: Xi Invites Taiwan’s Opposition Leader to First Visit in Decade

author: Hadriana Lowenkron
description: President Donald Trump said that Iran “gave” the US most of the 15 demands it sent to Tehran as demands for an end to the war, even as it remains unclear whether either side is really negotiating.
title: Trump Says Iran ‘Gave’ the US Most of Its Demands in Peace Plan
